definitions.explanation: The foremost line of a battle or conflict. Also used figuratively for the forefront of any activity or field.
A boundary between two air masses of different temperatures, as used in meteorology. Commonly heard in weather forecasts.

examples.japanese: {兵士|へいし}たちは{前線|ぜんせん}に{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: The soldiers were sent to the front line.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{研究|けんきゅう}の{最前線|さいぜんせん}で{活躍|かつやく}している。
examples.english: He is active at the forefront of research.

examples.japanese: {医療|いりょう}の{前線|ぜんせん}で{働|はたら}く{人|ひと}たちに{感謝|かんしゃ}したい。
examples.english: I want to thank the people working on the front lines of healthcare.

examples.japanese: {梅雨|つゆ}{前線|ぜんせん}が{近|ちか}づいている。
examples.english: The rainy season front is approaching.

examples.japanese: {前線|ぜんせん}の{影響|えいきょう}で{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}になる。
examples.english: Due to the weather front, it will rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: {停滞|ていたい}{前線|ぜんせん}が{日本|にほん}{列島|れっとう}の{上|うえ}に{長|なが}くとどまり、{各地|かくち}で{大雨|おおあめ}となった。
examples.english: A stationary front lingered over the Japanese archipelago, causing heavy rain across the country.

notes:
{前線|ぜんせん} has two main meanings: (1) the front line of battle or activity, and (2) a weather front in meteorology.

COMPOUNDS:
{前|ぜん} (front) + {線|せん} (line).

SENSE 1 — FRONT LINE:
Used literally for military contexts and figuratively for being at the forefront of any field.
- {最前線|さいぜんせん}: the very forefront
- {前線|ぜんせん}に{立|た}つ: to stand on the front line
- {医療|いりょう}の{前線|ぜんせん}: the front lines of healthcare

SENSE 2 — WEATHER FRONT:
A standard meteorology term heard daily in weather forecasts.
- {梅雨|つゆ}{前線|ぜんせん}: rainy season front
- {停滞|ていたい}{前線|ぜんせん}: stationary front
- {寒冷|かんれい}{前線|ぜんせん}: cold front
- {温暖|おんだん}{前線|ぜんせん}: warm front

USAGE:
The compound {最前線|さいぜんせん} (very forefront) is extremely common in both literal and figurative use: {研究|けんきゅう}の{最前線|さいぜんせん} (the cutting edge of research).
